findings.title: Unsubscribe mutates state on a GET request (CSRF / link-prefetch)
findings.body: The new `unsubscribe` action is routed as GET (`get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` in config/routes.rb) and is added to `skip_before_filter :check_xhr`, so a plain browser GET with only the session cookie changes the user's TopicUser notification_level. This violates safe-GET semantics in two ways: (1) any third-party page can silently unsubscribe/mute a logged-in user from an arbitrary topic via `` since topic ids are enumerable; (2) mail clients and security scanners (Outlook SafeLinks, Gmail prefetch, corporate link checkers) routinely follow links in emails, so the unsubscribe link in the notification email can be triggered without the user ever clicking it, silently muting the topic. The mutation should require a POST/PUT with CSRF protection, with the GET page only rendering the confirmation UI.

findings.title: unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when the user has no TopicUser row
findings.body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil — any logged-in user can visit `/t/<id>/unsubscribe` for a topic they have never read, posted in, or been emailed about, in which case no topic_users row exists. The very next line calls `tu.notification_level`, raising NoMethodError and producing a 500. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic.id, notification_level: ...)` (which upserts) or handle the nil case explicitly.

findings.title: topicUnsubscribe route is shadowed by topic.fromParamsNear wildcard
findings.body: The new route `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', { path: '/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe' })` is declared after `this.resource('topic', { path: '/t/:slug/:id' }, ...)` whose child route `fromParamsNear` has path `/:nearPost`. Ember matches routes in declaration order, so `/t/some-slug/123/unsubscribe` matches `topic.fromParamsNear` with `nearPost = "unsubscribe"` and the topicUnsubscribe route is never reached. The client then runs topic-from-params' setupController with a garbage nearPost, loading the topic stream instead of the unsubscribe confirmation page. The route must be declared before the topic resource (or nested with an explicit path that takes precedence).

findings.title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires unsubscribe_url; callers without it will raise
findings.body: config/locales/server.en.yml changed `unsubscribe_link` to include `[click here](%{unsubscribe_url})`. MessageBuilder calls `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` (here and in html_part) whenever `add_unsubscribe_link` is true, but `unsubscribe_url` is only present in template_args if the caller passed it. Any existing or future caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` will now raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fail to build the email. Either make the interpolation optional (fall back to the old text when unsubscribe_url is absent) or guard it in MessageBuilder.

findings.title: Direct TopicUser save bypasses bookkeeping done by TopicUser.change
findings.body: The unsubscribe action sets `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!` directly instead of using `TopicUser.change`. As a result `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` are not updated (so there is no audit trail of when/why the level changed) and no MessageBus `notification_level_change` event is published, leaving the user's other open browser tabs showing a stale notification state for the topic.

findings.title: No request specs for the new topics#unsubscribe action
findings.body: The PR adds a new state-changing controller action (notification level changes, slug-mismatch 301 redirect, nil-TopicUser case, login requirement) but the only spec change is adding an `unsubscribe_url` option to an existing message builder spec. There are no request/controller specs covering the unsubscribe flow, which is how the nil TopicUser crash and the GET-mutation behavior slipped through.
